metadata.release_gate_for: P25 — pins the Improvement-log entry format in process SKILL.md §5
metadata.baseline_note: without_skill baseline intentionally skipped: this is the release-gate iteration (regression detection) for a §5 wording change, not a skill-value study. The value study is the documented, still-unrun baseline-arm procedure in README.

notes: Contract `car-valuation` v1, 11 numbered fixed Rules, Improvement log empty at creation.
Executor extended the existing DATA.md Schema with the new target instead of duplicating a strategy — correct §1 behavior, same as the 2026-07-29 iteration.
Fixed the valuation constants deterministically (base price, verdict bands, mileage slope) and flagged each for maturation, as eval mode requires.

DATA.md written before the contract ('a process that cannot say where its results go is not done'), with the store inferred from evidence (no DATABASE_URL, no ORM, no compose db service; the sibling contract's `persistence: git-markdown:` clinched it).

Contract `letter-triplet-counts` v1 put the derived table in its own file so recomputes never touch the protected source table — beyond the assertions, consistent with the no-destructive-ops convention.

THE POINT OF THIS ITERATION: the Improvement-log assertion passes against the RE-TIGHTENED grader, which now requires '^### <YYYY-MM-DD>'. In the 2026-07-29 iteration the executor emitted a dated bullet and the grader had to be loosened to accept any dated line; with process SKILL.md §5 pinning the format (P25), the executor produced `### 2026-07-30 — added round_number boolean …` unprompted. The v0.32.0 follow-up is closed by fixing the skill, not the grader.
Version bumped 1 → 2; original Rule 1 (Normalize) preserved; round_number added to Rules, Output schema, Persistence and Guardrails (derived-never-judged, so it stays out of Judgment latitude).
Executor also migrated the datastore header and backfilled the one seeded row additively — no row or rejection deleted.
Release gate for v0.34.0: 3/3 evals green, 39/39 assertions, no grader changes needed this iteration — the opposite of 2026-07-29, where the grader had to be loosened.
Graders verified red on the untouched fixture before the runs (all three eval ids).
Total cost: ~133.4k subagent tokens, 38 tool calls, 1 run per eval.
n=1 per eval. Adequate as a regression gate; not a statistical result.
Executors were instructed not to read skills/process/evals/ so the grading criteria could not leak into the runs.
